bundled_design.rule: one binary choice per product category per respondent (never the same category twice, in any format); pair within category dealt by EvenPresentation; the presentation order of the choice pages randomized (SubSet=K EvenPresentation block randomizer); trial slot t is a CATEGORY coordinate, not a presentation position
bundled_design.wave1_arithmetic: the binding categories carry 4 pairs, so n per pair = participants/4; 400/4 = 100 on the 4-pair categories; 2-pair categories get participants/2; single-pair categories get every respondent (CALIBRATION_DESIGN wave procedure, 2026-07-01)

geometry_items.question_text: Look at the lettered options above. Is any one option clearly worse than another option on every feature listed? If so, which one?
choices: Yes — Option A is clearly worse than another option on every feature
Yes — Option B is clearly worse than another option on every feature
Yes — Option C is clearly worse than another option on every feature
No — every option is better than each other option on at least one feature
geometry_items.correct_choice_label: Yes — Option B is clearly worse than another option on every feature

geometry_items.question_text: Look at the three options above. On which feature do the options differ by the widest amount (the largest gap between the lowest and the highest value)?
choices: The features differ by about the same amount

geometry_items.question_text: One of the options above is marked currently unavailable. Compared with the other options, that unavailable option is:
choices: Better on one feature and equal or worse on the rest
Exactly the same as another option
geometry_items.correct_choice_label: Better on one feature and equal or worse on the rest

geometry_items.question_text: Look at the lettered options above. Which option is the most premium one (the highest-end option, with the most capability at the highest price)?
Look at the three options above. Is any one option clearly worse than both of the other two options?
choices: Yes, one option is worse than both of the others
No option is worse than both others
geometry_items.correct_choice_label: Yes, one option is worse than both of the others

geometry_items.question_text: The options above fall into groups by quality level. How many distinct quality levels (tiers) do you see among the options?
Look at the three options above. Are any two of the options nearly identical to each other (almost the same on every feature)?
choices: Yes, two options are nearly identical
No, all three options are clearly different
geometry_items.correct_choice_label: Yes, two options are nearly identical

terminal_lock_criterion.rule: LOCK when the wave-3 point estimate is in [40, 45]; OR the 95% CI overlaps [40, 45] AND the point estimate is in [33, 50] (target disadvantaged and non-extreme). Fail -> the pre-registered stimulus-defect contingencies, reported. Fixed 2026-07-02 in CALIBRATION_DESIGN's wave-3 amendment (a), BEFORE any wave-3 data.

per_arm_values_note: WAVE 3 (amendment (b)): values are PER-ARM — the recorded departure from wave-2's shared values (the same shared values landed 24.8-84.8% across one category's format arms). Trustworthy two-point price solves on 4 arms; conservative single QUALITY steps on the wrong-signed/extrapolation-only arms; water_bottles format arms unchanged. Full per-arm trail in arm_value_overrides_applied and pretest/wave3_pairs.json.

enrichment.spec: amendment (c): adjustable tiers only; per option a brand-neutral numeral-free model name + per attribute the canonical render_value string verbatim + one plain-language numeral-free non-comparative qualifier; ONE content source (stimuli/enrich.py + the kit) feeds numbers/words/pictures; pictures use the <sid>_wave3.png enriched re-renders with the attribute-naming legend (the wave-2 water-bottles legend fix); tier-1 never enriched (none dealt).

geometry_wave3.host_rationale: amendment (d): robot_vacuums locked in wave 2 and is dealt to NO ONE as a wave-3 choice, so geometry items never share a category with the respondent's choices; its cells rebuild in memory from the LOCKED anchor = the values respondents will actually judge after G3 (decoy target = HD per the R3-2C counterbalance map)
geometry_wave3.deal: 42 ordered structure-pairs (7x6, i != j), one EvenPresentation SubSet=1 randomizer; each structure appears in 12/42 pairs -> n = 2N/7 per structure, position counterbalanced (6 first / 6 second)

frq_margin.basis: the ONE final registered margin-strengthening correction (second-miss rule): FRQ 61% -> 44% after clarification; decoy now 5,000 Pa / $624.99 vs the 6,000 Pa / $499.99 target - visibly worse on both

rng_extension.basis: same registered correction on RNG's lever (51% -> 59% at the corrected key): range extension amplified x1.7 -> x2.2 of the target's price; decoy 6,000 Pa / $1,099.98

geometry_wave3.unchanged_structures: SOT stimulus untouched (wave-2 miss = 2 answers short, CI straddling 70); PHT/SYM/MOT/SIM untouched; all items keep the v2.2 wording + card presentation so the re-check isolates the margin change; keys computed from the built cells
geometry_wave3.g3_note: the strengthened FRQ/RNG parameters enter geometry.py as explicit arguments and are adopted by the confirmatory stimuli only at the G3 rebuild under the freeze protocol
geometry_wave3.deal_realized: 42 ordered structure-pairs (7x6) under one EvenPresentation SubSet=1 randomizer; fields geo1_*/geo2_*; per-structure n = 2N/7 (132 nominal at N=462); position counterbalanced (each structure leads in 6 pairs, trails in 6).

pic_comprehension.status: DESCRIPTIVE comprehension indicator for the pictures manipulation (amendment (e)); shown only when >=1 pictures pair was dealt (display logic over the pictures-capable slots); the key (Option B = the higher-quality HD option under the canonical order) is asserted from the effective values at build time; NOT a registered gate.

wave3_deal.arithmetic: 9 categories carry unlocked arms (robot_vacuums locked in wave 2) -> 9 choices per respondent; binding 3-arm categories get 462/3 = 154 nominal (>=150 kept at the observed 1.0-2.5% exclusion rates); water_bottles 231; singles 462; geometry 2 items/respondent -> 462*2/7 = 132 nominal per structure (~129 kept). The $700 cap invoked the pre-stated geometry n>=120 relief (7x150 kept needs ~539 respondents ~= $812). Session component-built on the wave-2 REALIZED medians (255 s total; 9.6 s/choice; 33.8 s geometry page): ~5.0-5.3 min -> pay $1.13 = $696.11 all-in ($12.7-14.1/hr across the honest range; protocol language $12-15/hr; the author confirms session + pay at launch per the standing rule; alternative $1.25 = $770.04 if the cap is relaxed).

items.static: locked category (wave 2), not dealt as a wave-3 choice: baked context at the locked values with the enriched description

realism_check.threshold: mean >= 5.0 and no recurring confusion in comments (CALIBRATION_DESIGN step 1)
realism_check.ordering_deviation: the registered procedure put the ~60-rater realism check BEFORE the calibration wave; wave 1 fielded without it (deviation flagged in CALIBRATION_WAVE1 s4). The check rides IN wave 2 instead — every wave-2 respondent rates all three invented categories' product pages at the values they were shown — and the invented categories' values lock only after BOTH the wave-2 shares and the realism verdicts are in. Documented honestly in the Stage-1 pre-testing trail.

exc_handling: EXC carries NO calibration pair and NO geometry item: it is built from MOT (exc_from_mot) and re-derived from the LOCKED MOT tiers at G3 (build_stimuli.py -> validate_stimuli.py), so it inherits MOT's calibrated tiers; the MOT tier-distinctness check serves both menus (CALIBRATION_DESIGN EXC re-derivation step).
recruitment_note: Calibration sample is INDEPENDENT of the confirmatory samples: a Prolific exclusion allowlist excludes calibration participants from the four main studies; calibration responses never enter confirmatory analyses (CALIBRATION_DESIGN).
